title: Machine-learning metabolomics prioritizes serum metabolites for SLE diagnosis and activity assessment
summary: Targeted serum metabolomics compared 89 patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and 44 healthy participants, identifying 146 differential metabolites. The authors combined statistical screening with seven machine-learning models to prioritize eight diagnostic biomarker candidates (reported AUCs above 0.95). Two additional metabolites, N-methyl-L-glutamic acid and L-2-aminobutyric acid, were evaluated by ELISA in a 90-patient SLE validation cohort and associated with SLE Disease Activity Index scores.
ai_technology: Seven machine-learning classification models applied to targeted serum metabolomics
organization: The Affiliated Guangzhou Panyu Central Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University; Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine; Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University; Panyu District Central Hospital

evidence.tested: The authors combined statistical screening with seven machine-learning models to prioritize eight diagnostic biomarker candidates (reported AUCs above 0.95).
evidence.unknown: This retrospective case-control study has modest cohorts and does not establish a clinically deployed test, causal SLE mechanism, or patient benefit. Reported diagnostic AUCs and SLEDAI associations require independent prospective replication; the validation cohort described in the abstract consists of SLE patients and does not by itself establish performance against a new external healthy/control population. The authors’ pathway interpretation is hypothesis-generating.
evidence.ai_role: The study iteratively compared seven machine-learning models to select candidate metabolites for SLE classification and combined the selected features with statistical screening. N-methyl-L-glutamic acid and L-2-aminobutyric acid were subsequently assessed by ELISA in a patient validation cohort; the machine-learning analysis nominated candidates, while the assays supplied biological measurement follow-up.
